writer: claude-opus-5-5 (written by hand in Claude Code)
summary: Sibling relationships are often the longest-lasting relationships in a person's life. Siblings usually spend more time together in childhood than with parents or anyone else, and their bond tends to be more equal than ties across generations. In industrialized cultures the relationship is usually optional, while in nonindustrialized cultures close sibling ties are often obligatory. The bond is fairly stable through childhood. Adolescence often brings more conflict and distance, and intimacy usually returns in young adulthood. Siblings influence each other much as peers do: warm relationships support healthy development, while conflict and aggression can promote delinquency. Adult siblings often stay in touch, especially sisters and those who live close to each other. Sibling rivalry is common and often comes from competing for parents' attention. One child psychologist says it is most intense when children are close in age and of the same gender.
